elements.element: Customer is not liable to pay any liquidated damages under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that “Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages.”

elements.element: Customer is not liable to pay any penalties under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that “Customer shall not be liable for any ... penalties under this Agreement.”

elements.element: If any liquidated amount is payable by Customer, it may arise only as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause eliminates all liquidated amounts payable by Customer.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee constituting a liquidated amount is capped at three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer cannot be liable for any liquidated amount, including an early-termination fee; zero liability is below the three-month cap.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than the permitted early-termination fee is payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause is stricter than this exclusivity requirement because it prohibits every liquidated amount payable by Customer.

result.reason: The operative redline cleanly replaces the punitive late-payment liquidated-damages provision with the preferred complete prohibition on liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. It therefore also satisfies the less protective fallback by eliminating the triggering liability entirely. The change is limited to the targeted risk and introduces no unrelated obligation or apparent contradiction.
